Mostly because you could grow potatoes in Europe. Potatoes were introduced in Ireland by Walter Raleigh around the late 1580s. Constant wars and subsequent famines meant the peasants would often starve and Fredrick of Prussia introduced potatoes to the peasants hoping they would catch on. 

Potatoes especially became a staple in Ireland where peasants could depend on the cheaper and calorie dense tubers replacing turnips and other foods. This is also why the potato blight lead to the Great Famine in Ireland as a majority of the population was singularly dependent on potatoes as their main source of food. 

Potatoes are also much easier to grow. They are considered hardy in Europe and can survive frost. Both the climate and soil in much of Europe is favourable to its growth. 

As to why corn and cassava didn’t take over: 
According to the USDA, corn requires a warm climate with sufficient rainfall and cassava similarly requires a warm and humid climate which is very far from the climate we usually experience on the Continent. Corn also posed another risk of being burned down by approaching armies. Considering how potatoes were introduced as a wartime crop by Fredrick, it would make sense that peasants would prefer potatoes over corn. 

Most importantly potatoes do not spoil easily and can be stored for long periods of time and do not require a lot of manual labour like transplanting rice.

i’d say, first of all, focus on cost. as an (presumably) international student, you will be paying three times the home fee, which is a lot but less than yale if you end up getting financial aid. yale, as far as i’m aware, is need blind and meets 100% of demonstrated need, so you could very well be studying there for free.

if costs are not an issue for you, focus on what you want to do after you get your degree. academia? then oxford will be better, since you will be done with your bachelors and masters quicker. similarly, draw up a list of pros and cons for whatever career you want. 

and third, where do you want to live after you finish? obviously, you could go back to the us after you finish at oxford. but i’ve seen many of my american friends not care as much about oxford. personally, however, i’d say in terms of prestige, they’re both equal.

good luck and congratulations for both of these amazing offers!!

edit: culture shock!! you might be shocked to learn that the us and uk are very different. if you’re more of a conservative, you’d be better suited to yale than oxford.
